text:
On the morning of 14 September, the fields of the Tavrin Valley stood pale and thin under a low sky, the barley heads light enough to bend at a breath of wind. For generations the valley has measured its year by this crop, which has filled its granaries and shaped its calendar of sowing and threshing.

That reckoning turned grim when the Tavrin Valley Agricultural Board declared the barley harvest a failure. Its "Autumn Harvest Assessment Report No. 7," released alongside an emergency session of the Valley Council, found yields 61% below the five-year seasonal average, with roughly 18,400 hectares affected.

Dr. Ilsa Marenko, the Board's Chief Crop Assessor, oversaw the findings. The valley has weathered lean seasons before, but few have been recorded so starkly. What follows will be tested in the months ahead.
